gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-inria-sans: Bold, bendy shapes up top, then calm copper-pipe curves below. Bellota Text has no calligraphic shading, so Inria Sans follows with tubular strokes and see-through c openings that keep a long page of sans-serif text feeling modern and easy.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-istok-web: Chunky, confident letters lead in Bellota Text, every stroke the same weight, while Istok Web brings rounded sans shapes with a clearly open side. Paragraphs feel friendly.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-jost: Wide-open, commanding display type. Bellota Text sets the tone with no shading at all, and Jost carries on in a plain sans with broad terminal gaps and a unit-width stroke, which keeps long reading tidy.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-jura: Distinctive and unshaded, Bellota Text opens its c, e and s shapes wide for a commanding heading. And Jura, a plain sans with wire-constant strokes and s curves open at both ends, is the one that quietly handles the text.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-k2d: K2D carries a tube-like thickness through every bend, with c terminals hanging far from the bowl. But Bellota Text is the one with presence, open and unshaded and built to command a heading, while the sans handles the text.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-kanchenjunga: Bellota Text makes a distinctive, commanding entrance with open c, e and s shapes and no calligraphic shading. And Kanchenjunga, a sans with the steady line of a drafting pen, earns its keep elsewhere, since Bellota Text is best big and short.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-kantumruy-pro: Approachable from the first line, with Bellota Text drawing unshaded, open shapes. Kantumruy Pro follows in sans-serif, its e opening clearly to the right and its hairline-free letterforms making a long page easy going.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-koho: Open, unshaded curves with no stress in them lead in Bellota Text. And KoHo, a sans-serif with wide c apertures, sits underneath so the heading and the text feel like one friendly voice.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-kosugi: Kosugi has an open-jawed c like a pair of pliers. Bellota Text is the better one for commanding headings with its unshaded, distinctive shapes, while the sans-serif Kosugi is best at the wire-bent text below.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-kosugi-maru: Kosugi Maru reads like neon tubing, stroke ends set far apart. Under Bellota Text's open, unshaded heading, the sans text moves along in one steady line thickness, so a long paragraph glides.
